//: Firebase Hosting config. The headers block is the important part.
By default Hosting serves static assets with Cache-Control: max-age=3600,
so for up to an hour after a deploy your browser keeps running the OLD
JavaScript and you see none of the changes. Worse, an ES module graph is
cached per-file, so a plain reload can leave you on a mix of new and old.
These rules make the browser revalidate the app code on every load (a
304 when nothing changed, so it stays fast) while letting the logo cache

If you deploy somewhere other than Firebase Hosting, this file is ignored
and you should set the equivalent headers there.
